outcome: The authoring wall now canonicalizes executable source into the Rust-accepted IR boundary before an Experiment can be treated as valid
owner_impact: Ordinary Controller and Metrics aliases such as a local name for obs.neighbours or snapshot.agents remain natural to write, but they are lowered away before execution. The exact Controller pattern that previously passed MCP validation and then failed in Rust now compiles to Rust-valid canonical IR. Controller validation also requires an unconditional action return, preventing a zero-neighbour runtime crash from being certified as valid. No scientific capability was added and candidate capabilities remain unavailable.

next.text: Next is #371, the fresh black-box blocking and two-paper acceptance rerun. It will retest the hard wall first, then candidate reuse/generalization across fresh paper sessions. It has not restarted yet.

technical_evidence: Browser and MCP Controller compilers are mirrored and lower neighbour-list aliases to canonical obs.neighbours IR.
Browser and MCP Metrics compilers are mirrored and lower snapshot.agents plus loop-agent aliases to Rust-executable canonical bindings.
Controller validation in both JavaScript and Rust now requires an unconditional top-level action return.
Regression coverage includes the exact production Controller pattern that exposed #380 and a basic syntax/mathematics matrix for Controller and Metrics.
All persisted source-changing MCP paths continue to use the shared authoring validator.
No scientific capability, candidate availability, MCP tool count, CI/CD rule, retry/timeout behavior, or development workflow changed.
